summary: Configured node1 via Ansible to run /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker as systemd service inventory-worker under dedicated inventorysvc system account. Verified service is active/enabled and running as inventorysvc. Completed mandatory restart protocol on both node1 and node2, confirming changed boot IDs and full recovery of the service and cluster after each restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: confirmed Ubuntu 24.04, ansible pre-installed, worker binary present, no pre-existing inventorysvc user or inventory-worker service
Created local inventory (localhost, ansible_connection=local) and an Ansible playbook at /tmp/ansible-inventory-worker/playbook.yml on node1

Playbook creates system group/user 'inventorysvc' (nologin shell, dedicated home), ensures worker binary is executable, installs /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service running ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker as User/Group=inventorysvc, reloads systemd, enables and starts the service
Ran playbook with ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini playbook.yml (become: true) — 4 changed tasks, 0 failed
Verified idempotency by re-running playbook (0 changed)
Verified inventory-worker service active/enabled and process running under uid 999 (inventorysvc)
Captured pre-restart baseline boot_id/uptime and service state on node1, and boot_id/uptime on node2

Restarted node1 via 'sudo systemctl reboot' (backgrounded so ack returned before disconnect), polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed (96c08b66... -> b94c9b1d...) with uptime ~6s, verified inventory-worker service came back active/enabled and running as inventorysvc
Restarted node2 via 'sudo systemctl reboot', polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed (a6937a34... -> f85e9d2d...) with uptime ~3.7s, verified system-is-running=running
Final re-check confirmed inventory-worker still active/enabled on node1 after both node restarts

evidence.requirement: os-comparison-worker runs as managed service 'inventory-worker' under dedicated 'inventorysvc' account, implemented via Ansible
evidence.summary: Baseline showed no inventorysvc user or inventory-worker unit; Ansible playbook (local connection) created the system user/group, systemd unit, and enabled+started the service; verification showed inventory-worker active/enabled with MainPID process running as uid 999 (inventorysvc); rerun was idempotent (0 changed)

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered service
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 96c08b66-... with service active/enabled; systemctl reboot acknowledged and backgrounded; subsequent connection timed out confirming disconnect; polling recovered with new boot_id b94c9b1d-... and uptime ~6s; inventory-worker confirmed active/enabled and running as inventorysvc post-reboot; final re-check still active/enabled

evidence.requirement: node2 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered node health
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id a6937a34-...; systemctl reboot acknowledged and backgrounded; subsequent connection timed out confirming disconnect; polling recovered with new boot_id f85e9d2d-... and uptime ~3.7s; systemctl is-system-running reported 'running' confirming node health post-reboot
